changedFields.before: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and three imperial grandsons to Jinyong with armed guards, interrogated Consort-in-chief Xie and heir guardian Jiang Jun to death.
changedFields.after: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong City with armed soldiers, and had Consort Shufei Xie and Jiang Jun, a baolin of the crown prince, interrogated to death.
changedFields.reason: 以兵仗送 describes Dan escorting with armed force; it does not specify that he sent guards without going. 考竟 is interrogation to death and 保林 is a rank, not an heir guardian.

changedFields.before: Dan marched Wang consort and grandsons to Jinyong—executed Xie and Jiang Jun.
changedFields.after: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong City under armed guard, and had Consort Shufei Xie and Jiang Jun, a crown prince’s consort of the rank of baolin, interrogated to death.
changedFields.reason: The source says Dan escorted them with armed force, not that he sent guards separately. 考竟 specifies interrogation to death; the rank 保林 is not an heir guardian.

changedFields.before: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi Ce to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
changedFields.after: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and restored the crown prince by patent, saying: 'The emperor sends an envoy bearing the tally, Commandant of the Guard Yi, concurrently serving as Director of Works, to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
changedFields.reason: 伊 is the name of the envoy; 策 is the patent action and is not part of his name. 兼司空 and 衛尉 identify his offices.

changedFields.before: In youth you bore a nature quick and wise; the late emperor gave you exceptional favor, opening great territory, holding Hailing.
changedFields.after: In youth you bore a nature quick and wise; you received the late emperor’s extraordinary favor. Your domain was greatly opened, and you came to possess Huailing.
changedFields.reason: 淮陵 is Huailing, not Hailing. The parallel phrases describe the opening of the domain and possession of Huailing without explicitly assigning both actions to the late emperor.

changedFields.before: Hui's ghost-eulogy praised Wu Di's love and Yu's fief.
changedFields.after: From youth you showed remarkable intelligence and received the late emperor’s extraordinary favor. Your domain was greatly expanded, and you came to possess Huailing.
changedFields.reason: The speech directly addresses the deceased, and 淮陵 is Huailing. The source does not explicitly say that the late emperor personally granted both territorial actions.

changedFields.before: In the fourth month posthumous investiture as Prince of Nanyang.
changedFields.after: In the fourth month, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang.
changedFields.reason: 追封 means posthumous enfeoffment; 四月 gives the fourth month. The preceding unit identifies the deceased subject, although its missing written name remains a separate source issue.

changedFields.before: Fourth month titled Prince of Nanyang.
changedFields.after: In the fourth month, he was posthumously made Prince of Nanyang.
changedFields.reason: 追封 is a posthumous grant of title. The preceding unit provides the deceased subject; this decision does not repair or settle its missing name.
